definitions.explanation: The punctuation mark (.) used to end a sentence, primarily in Western-language contexts. In Japanese typography, the equivalent is the 句点 (くてん).
Used figuratively to mean putting a definitive end to something, such as a relationship, conflict, or era. Almost always appears in the phrase 終止符を打つ.

examples.japanese: {文|ぶん}の{終|お}わりに{終止符|しゅうしふ}を{打|う}つ。
examples.english: Put a period at the end of a sentence.

examples.japanese: {英語|えいご}では{文末|ぶんまつ}にピリオドという{終止符|しゅうしふ}を{使|つか}う。
examples.english: In English, a period is used at the end of a sentence.

examples.japanese: {終止符|しゅうしふ}の{位置|いち}が{正|ただ}しいか{確認|かくにん}してください。
examples.english: Please check whether the period is in the correct position.

examples.japanese: {長|なが}い{争|あらそ}いに{終止符|しゅうしふ}を{打|う}った。
examples.english: They put an end to the long dispute.

examples.japanese: この{判決|はんけつ}で{事件|じけん}に{終止符|しゅうしふ}が{打|う}たれた。
examples.english: This ruling brought the case to a close.

examples.japanese: {二人|ふたり}の{関係|かんけい}に{終止符|しゅうしふ}を{打|う}つ{決心|けっしん}をした。
examples.english: I made up my mind to put an end to our relationship.

notes:
Composed of {終止|しゅうし} (ending, termination) + {符|ふ} (mark, sign).

LITERAL SENSE:
Refers to a period/full stop (.) in Western-language punctuation. The Japanese equivalent is {句点|くてん} (。).

FIGURATIVE SENSE:
Much more commonly used in the figurative sense of "putting a definitive end to something." Almost always appears in the set expression {終止符|しゅうしふ}を{打|う}つ.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {終止符|しゅうしふ}を{打|う}つ: to put an end to; to bring to a close
- {終止符|しゅうしふ}が{打|う}たれる: to be brought to an end (passive)
- 〜に{終止符|しゅうしふ}を{打|う}つ: to put an end to 〜

USAGE:
- {争|あらそ}いに{終止符|しゅうしふ}を{打|う}つ: to end a dispute
- {関係|かんけい}に{終止符|しゅうしふ}を{打|う}つ: to end a relationship
- {時代|じだい}に{終止符|しゅうしふ}を{打|う}つ: to bring an era to a close
